rules.text: Apply this recommendation only when ALL requirements hold: The answer must be YES: Is the adult patient living with chronic kidney disease (including non-dialysis CKD stages 1–5, haemodialysis, or kidney transplant recipient)? AND The answer must be YES: Is the patient currently receiving haemodialysis? AND The answer must be YES: Does the haemodialysis patient have any uncontrolled or clinically unstable medical condition that would represent a contraindication to exercise (e.g., infection or fever, recent myocardial infarction within 2 weeks, undiagnosed chest pain, resting systolic blood pressure > 200 mmHg, resting diastolic blood pressure > 110 mmHg, symptomatic hyper- or hypotension, or other conditions that could be aggravated by exercise as per American Heart Association/American College of Sports Medicine Class D)?. Recommendation: Do not initiate or progress structured exercise or intradialytic exercise at this time; manage unstable condition first and follow standard haemodialysis care without added exercise.

Apply this recommendation only when ALL requirements hold: The answer must be YES: Is the adult patient living with chronic kidney disease (including non-dialysis CKD stages 1–5, haemodialysis, or kidney transplant recipient)? AND The answer must be YES: Is the patient currently receiving haemodialysis? AND The answer must be NO: Does the haemodialysis patient have any uncontrolled or clinically unstable medical condition that would represent a contraindication to exercise (e.g., infection or fever, recent myocardial infarction within 2 weeks, undiagnosed chest pain, resting systolic blood pressure > 200 mmHg, resting diastolic blood pressure > 110 mmHg, symptomatic hyper- or hypotension, or other conditions that could be aggravated by exercise as per American Heart Association/American College of Sports Medicine Class D)? AND The answer must be YES: Is intradialytic cycling exercise during haemodialysis available in the unit (equipment and at least minimal staff resource to supervise)? AND The answer must be YES: Is the patient within approximately the first 30 minutes of the haemodialysis session?. Recommendation: Delay starting intradialytic cycling until after the first 30 minutes of haemodialysis, then perform supervised intradialytic cycling for at least 30 minutes at a moderate intensity (Borg RPE 12–14) on each haemodialysis treatment (3 times/week), and encourage additional physical activity on non-dialysis days aiming toward a total of 150 minutes/week of moderate activity (or 75 minutes vigorous).

Apply this recommendation only when ALL requirements hold: The answer must be YES: Is the adult patient living with chronic kidney disease (including non-dialysis CKD stages 1–5, haemodialysis, or kidney transplant recipient)? AND The answer must be YES: Is the patient currently receiving haemodialysis? AND The answer must be NO: Does the haemodialysis patient have any uncontrolled or clinically unstable medical condition that would represent a contraindication to exercise (e.g., infection or fever, recent myocardial infarction within 2 weeks, undiagnosed chest pain, resting systolic blood pressure > 200 mmHg, resting diastolic blood pressure > 110 mmHg, symptomatic hyper- or hypotension, or other conditions that could be aggravated by exercise as per American Heart Association/American College of Sports Medicine Class D)? AND The answer must be YES: Is intradialytic cycling exercise during haemodialysis available in the unit (equipment and at least minimal staff resource to supervise)? AND The answer must be NO: Is the patient within approximately the first 30 minutes of the haemodialysis session?. Recommendation: Provide supervised intradialytic cycling during this haemodialysis session for at least 30 minutes at a moderate intensity (Borg RPE 12–14) on each treatment (3 times/week) to improve cardiovascular health, physical function, muscular strength, blood pressure control, lipid profile and dialysis efficiency, and encourage additional interdialytic physical activity toward 150 minutes/week of moderate activity (or 75 minutes vigorous).

Apply this recommendation only when ALL requirements hold: The answer must be YES: Is the adult patient living with chronic kidney disease (including non-dialysis CKD stages 1–5, haemodialysis, or kidney transplant recipient)? AND The answer must be YES: Is the patient currently receiving haemodialysis? AND The answer must be NO: Does the haemodialysis patient have any uncontrolled or clinically unstable medical condition that would represent a contraindication to exercise (e.g., infection or fever, recent myocardial infarction within 2 weeks, undiagnosed chest pain, resting systolic blood pressure > 200 mmHg, resting diastolic blood pressure > 110 mmHg, symptomatic hyper- or hypotension, or other conditions that could be aggravated by exercise as per American Heart Association/American College of Sports Medicine Class D)? AND The answer must be NO: Is intradialytic cycling exercise during haemodialysis available in the unit (equipment and at least minimal staff resource to supervise)?. Recommendation: Encourage haemodialysis patient to perform regular physical activity outside dialysis (e.g. home-based walking or other moderate-intensity activity) aiming for 150 minutes/week of moderate intensity (or 75 minutes vigorous, or a mixture), with programmes ideally supervised by appropriately qualified staff when available, while addressing individual patient and staff barriers to optimise participation and adherence.

Apply this recommendation only when ALL requirements hold: The answer must be YES: Is the adult patient living with chronic kidney disease (including non-dialysis CKD stages 1–5, haemodialysis, or kidney transplant recipient)? AND The answer must be NO: Is the patient currently receiving haemodialysis? AND The answer must be YES: Has the patient received a kidney transplant (kidney transplant recipient, including candidates and post-transplant)? AND The answer must be YES: Does the kidney transplant recipient (KTR) have any contraindications or safety concerns for exercise (e.g., situations where traumatic damage to the transplanted kidney, participation in contact sports, prolonged extreme exercise, or use of sport-enhancing supplements is being considered without specialist input)?. Recommendation: Avoid contact sports and activities with high risk of traumatic graft damage, avoid prolonged extreme endurance events unless carefully considered with a transplant and sports medicine team, and avoid sport‑enhancing dietary supplements; otherwise encourage only moderate, non-contact physical activity within standard guidelines.

Apply this recommendation only when ALL requirements hold: The answer must be YES: Is the adult patient living with chronic kidney disease (including non-dialysis CKD stages 1–5, haemodialysis, or kidney transplant recipient)? AND The answer must be NO: Is the patient currently receiving haemodialysis? AND The answer must be YES: Has the patient received a kidney transplant (kidney transplant recipient, including candidates and post-transplant)? AND The answer must be NO: Does the kidney transplant recipient (KTR) have any contraindications or safety concerns for exercise (e.g., situations where traumatic damage to the transplanted kidney, participation in contact sports, prolonged extreme exercise, or use of sport-enhancing supplements is being considered without specialist input)? AND The answer must be YES: Is the KTR currently in the immediate post-transplant period (< 1–2 days after transplantation)?. Recommendation: Do not implement additional intensive physiotherapy or structured exercise beyond standard early mobility encouragement; continue standard care mobilization without extra intensive exercise, as early intensive physiotherapy has not shown added benefit.

Apply this recommendation only when ALL requirements hold: The answer must be YES: Is the adult patient living with chronic kidney disease (including non-dialysis CKD stages 1–5, haemodialysis, or kidney transplant recipient)? AND The answer must be NO: Is the patient currently receiving haemodialysis? AND The answer must be YES: Has the patient received a kidney transplant (kidney transplant recipient, including candidates and post-transplant)? AND The answer must be NO: Does the kidney transplant recipient (KTR) have any contraindications or safety concerns for exercise (e.g., situations where traumatic damage to the transplanted kidney, participation in contact sports, prolonged extreme exercise, or use of sport-enhancing supplements is being considered without specialist input)? AND The answer must be NO: Is the KTR currently in the immediate post-transplant period (< 1–2 days after transplantation)? AND The answer must be YES: Is the patient in the pre-transplant waiting period (candidate awaiting kidney transplant)?. Recommendation: Offer prehabilitation: encourage and, if possible, supervise structured cardiovascular and strength exercise (at least 3 times per week) to increase pre-transplant physical activity levels and potentially aid recovery post-transplant, aiming for at least 150 minutes/week of moderate‑to‑vigorous physical activity (or 75 minutes vigorous).

Apply this recommendation only when ALL requirements hold: The answer must be YES: Is the adult patient living with chronic kidney disease (including non-dialysis CKD stages 1–5, haemodialysis, or kidney transplant recipient)? AND The answer must be NO: Is the patient currently receiving haemodialysis? AND The answer must be YES: Has the patient received a kidney transplant (kidney transplant recipient, including candidates and post-transplant)? AND The answer must be NO: Does the kidney transplant recipient (KTR) have any contraindications or safety concerns for exercise (e.g., situations where traumatic damage to the transplanted kidney, participation in contact sports, prolonged extreme exercise, or use of sport-enhancing supplements is being considered without specialist input)? AND The answer must be NO: Is the KTR currently in the immediate post-transplant period (< 1–2 days after transplantation)? AND The answer must be NO: Is the patient in the pre-transplant waiting period (candidate awaiting kidney transplant)? AND The answer must be YES: Is the KTR willing and able to participate in structured exercise sessions at least 3 times per week?. Recommendation: Implement a supervised, individualised structured exercise programme performed at least 3 times/week, including aerobic exercise at >60% of maximum (heart rate or VO2peak) and resistance training of upper and lower body at >60% 1-RM at least 2 times/week, progressing volume gradually, to enhance cardiorespiratory fitness, muscular strength, physical function, HDL levels and health-related quality of life while aiming for ≥150 minutes/week of moderate-to-vigorous physical activity.

Apply this recommendation only when ALL requirements hold: The answer must be YES: Is the adult patient living with chronic kidney disease (including non-dialysis CKD stages 1–5, haemodialysis, or kidney transplant recipient)? AND The answer must be NO: Is the patient currently receiving haemodialysis? AND The answer must be YES: Has the patient received a kidney transplant (kidney transplant recipient, including candidates and post-transplant)? AND The answer must be NO: Does the kidney transplant recipient (KTR) have any contraindications or safety concerns for exercise (e.g., situations where traumatic damage to the transplanted kidney, participation in contact sports, prolonged extreme exercise, or use of sport-enhancing supplements is being considered without specialist input)? AND The answer must be NO: Is the KTR currently in the immediate post-transplant period (< 1–2 days after transplantation)? AND The answer must be NO: Is the patient in the pre-transplant waiting period (candidate awaiting kidney transplant)? AND The answer must be NO: Is the KTR willing and able to participate in structured exercise sessions at least 3 times per week?. Recommendation: Encourage general physical activity toward 150 minutes/week of moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (or 75 minutes vigorous), aiming to reduce all‑cause and cardiovascular mortality and improve functional outcomes, and address individual barriers and activators to increase uptake; structured exercise can be advised but may be unsupervised or adapted to the patient’s circumstances.

Apply this recommendation only when ALL requirements hold: The answer must be YES: Is the adult patient living with chronic kidney disease (including non-dialysis CKD stages 1–5, haemodialysis, or kidney transplant recipient)? AND The answer must be NO: Is the patient currently receiving haemodialysis? AND The answer must be NO: Has the patient received a kidney transplant (kidney transplant recipient, including candidates and post-transplant)? AND The answer must be YES: Is the patient in the non-dialysis CKD stages 1–5 group (not on dialysis, not transplanted)? AND The answer must be YES: Does the non-dialysis CKD patient have contraindications to physical activity or unstable/uncontrolled comorbidities?. Recommendation: Do not prescribe progressive exercise beyond gentle activity; manage contraindications and stabilise comorbidities first, while offering only cautious basic physical activity as tolerated.

Apply this recommendation only when ALL requirements hold: The answer must be YES: Is the adult patient living with chronic kidney disease (including non-dialysis CKD stages 1–5, haemodialysis, or kidney transplant recipient)? AND The answer must be NO: Is the patient currently receiving haemodialysis? AND The answer must be NO: Has the patient received a kidney transplant (kidney transplant recipient, including candidates and post-transplant)? AND The answer must be YES: Is the patient in the non-dialysis CKD stages 1–5 group (not on dialysis, not transplanted)? AND The answer must be NO: Does the non-dialysis CKD patient have contraindications to physical activity or unstable/uncontrolled comorbidities? AND The answer must be YES: Is the non-dialysis CKD patient currently doing at least 150 minutes per week of moderate intensity aerobic activity (or 75 minutes vigorous, or equivalent combination)?. Recommendation: Advise the patient to maintain current aerobic activity levels (≥150 minutes/week moderate or 75 minutes vigorous), ensure participation in muscle strength, balance and flexibility activities on at least 2 days per week, and minimise sedentary time by breaking up prolonged sitting; a prescribed combination of aerobic and muscle strengthening should be used to improve or maintain muscle function, blood pressure, physical function, and quality of life.

Apply this recommendation only when ALL requirements hold: The answer must be YES: Is the adult patient living with chronic kidney disease (including non-dialysis CKD stages 1–5, haemodialysis, or kidney transplant recipient)? AND The answer must be NO: Is the patient currently receiving haemodialysis? AND The answer must be NO: Has the patient received a kidney transplant (kidney transplant recipient, including candidates and post-transplant)? AND The answer must be YES: Is the patient in the non-dialysis CKD stages 1–5 group (not on dialysis, not transplanted)? AND The answer must be NO: Does the non-dialysis CKD patient have contraindications to physical activity or unstable/uncontrolled comorbidities? AND The answer must be NO: Is the non-dialysis CKD patient currently doing at least 150 minutes per week of moderate intensity aerobic activity (or 75 minutes vigorous, or equivalent combination)?. Recommendation: Encourage the patient to gradually increase physical activity from current levels toward 150 minutes/week of moderate intensity aerobic activity (or 75 minutes vigorous, or combination), participate in daily physical activity, undertake strength, balance and flexibility activities at least 2 days per week, and break up prolonged sedentary periods with light activity or standing; use a prescribed combination of aerobic and muscle strengthening to improve muscle function, blood pressure, physical function, and health-related quality of life.

Apply this recommendation only when ALL requirements hold: The answer must be YES: Is the adult patient living with chronic kidney disease (including non-dialysis CKD stages 1–5, haemodialysis, or kidney transplant recipient)? AND The answer must be NO: Is the patient currently receiving haemodialysis? AND The answer must be NO: Has the patient received a kidney transplant (kidney transplant recipient, including candidates and post-transplant)? AND The answer must be NO: Is the patient in the non-dialysis CKD stages 1–5 group (not on dialysis, not transplanted)?. Recommendation: The patient does not fall into the specified CKD non-dialysis, haemodialysis, or transplant groups covered by this guideline; apply other appropriate clinical guidelines.

Apply this recommendation only when ALL requirements hold: The answer must be NO: Is the adult patient living with chronic kidney disease (including non-dialysis CKD stages 1–5, haemodialysis, or kidney transplant recipient)?. Recommendation: This guideline does not apply because the patient does not have chronic kidney disease or kidney replacement therapy.

input.patient: An adult patient with chronic kidney disease was evaluated in the context of a kidney transplant recipient and was not receiving haemodialysis. The transplant course was beyond the immediate post-transplant period, with transplantation having occurred 14 days earlier, and the patient was not in the pre-transplant waiting period. No contraindications or safety concerns for exercise were identified, with no plans for contact sports, prolonged extreme exercise, or use of sport-enhancing supplements without specialist input, and there were no concerns raised about traumatic risk to the transplanted kidney. However, the patient was not willing and able to participate in structured exercise sessions at least three times per week. The primary clinical focus was management.
